documents: Bill of lading or air waybill
Form B534, fully filled in and signed on every page
Passport photo page and signature page copy
Visa copy, or visa grant letter if no visa label
Contents list in English, including boxes you packed yourself
Your full home address in Australia (no PO box or work address)
Travel itinerary if you land after the ship arrives
dutyFree: Personal effects of citizens or long-stay/permanent visa holders who lived abroad 12+ months
Goods must arrive within 6 months of your own arrival
Antiques over 100 years old are duty free, but 10% GST applies
restricted: Cars need a Vehicle Import Approval before shipping; duty and 10% GST apply
Do not pack meat, dairy, eggs, seeds, herbs or spices
Clean bikes, garden tools, camping and sports gear of all soil and plant matter
Tobacco needs a Home Affairs permit; alcohol is charged high duty and GST
Firearms need state police approval and a permit before shipping
notes: Every household shipment gets a biosecurity inspection, with fees and possible delays
Full containers cannot be delivered straight to your home because of the inspection
Your goods can be cleared before you arrive in Australia
Scanned forms are fine, but electronic signatures are not accepted

documents: Signed copy of your passport photo page
Packing list with number of packages
Statutory declaration of no dangerous goods (air shipments)
Car registration and proof of ownership (if shipping a vehicle)
restricted: E-bikes, e-scooters and hoverboards cannot be exported
Electric and hybrid cars cannot go in containers; roll-on/roll-off space is scarce
No lithium batteries at all in air shipments
By sea, battery items must be 100 Wh or less, with the rating known
notes: Export papers must use exactly the same name as your passport
Check battery ratings on vacuums, power tools and gadgets before packing
